hypothesis: The R3 checkpoint plus a source-only terminal review instruction increases task-3 context recall by retaining genuinely relevant delivered adjacent test evidence, while preserving efficiency.
mechanism: Overlay only compact representation. Preserve R3 conditional handoff; append a generic user instruction to the terminal-review request. The existing terminal system and native evidence packet remain authoritative. No task IDs, source paths, source bytes, gold, or scorer changes.
arm: radical-ranked-acquisition with conditional handoff and terminal review overlay
sequence_rule: Run task 3 first. If fixed quality or token screen fails, stop. Only if task 3 passes, run task 2. No replacement or silent retry.
screen_rule: Task 3 Span-F1 >= 0.5125361243, File-F1 >= 0.8, tokens <= 261037. If it passes, task 2 Span/File-F1 = 1 and tokens <= 461176. Every dispatched call must have known usage and native export valid.
gold_boundary: Generation mounts source-only task and pinned repository data, not gold or reference patches. Native scoring follows sealed generation.
claim_ceiling: Exposed development tasks under a configured 1M window; no full-cohort or occupied-deep-window generalization.
open_questions: Will the terminal review include useful adjacent test evidence?
Can task 3 beat the quality gate?
Will task 2 preserve perfect precision and recall if task 3 passes?
